chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Pianist Duke Brooks and bassist Iggy Shavack
summary: Remembering pianist Duke Brooks and bassist Iggy Shavack.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I'd like to mention a piano player who was a terrific guy and a fantastic piano player. His name was Duke Brooks. And he recorded with me later. I'll get into that later, but I wanted to make sure I mentioned his name. He was killed hoboing back to Kansas City to see his mother, on the train, and he fell off the train and it chopped him up, you know. But he was some pianist. Had a great feeling, a
great touch, you know. He really played loose, you know; very loose and warm on the piano.
Yeah, he was around on the scene during that particular time.

And Iggy Shavack(?), the bass player... Iggy was a very fine bassist on the scene at the time. He was one of the first guys that came through who really was singing on the bass, where the strings were singing, you know, around that time.
